text:
sara-acme: Hey team — our daily usage CSV export for org `acme-inc` is misaligned with the Console charts. The CSV marks ~2.4k tokens on 2024-03-12 but in the Console those same requests show up under 2024-03-11. Our org timezone is Asia/Tokyo (UTC+9). This is causing a mismatch in the daily billing slice.

maya (support): Thanks for the report, Sara. Can you paste a tiny sample of the exported CSV rows (timestamps + tokens) and confirm whether you used the Console export or the /v1/usage/export API?

sara-acme: Pasted small snippet below — exported from Console > Billing > Usage exports (scheduled export). We definitely have org timezone set to Asia/Tokyo in Org settings.

```
org_id,request_id,timestamp,model,tokens
acme-inc,req_001,2024-03-11T15:05:12Z,gpt-4,120
acme-inc,req_002,2024-03-11T23:58:01Z,gpt-4,230
acme-inc,req_003,2024-03-12T00:10:34Z,gpt-4,95
```

sara-acme: In the CSV above those three rows are dated 2024-03-12 (CSV day column = date(truncated to midnight) = 2024-03-12) but in our Console daily chart they are bucketed on 2024-03-11 (which is what we expect for Asia/Tokyo). So the CSV is inconsistent.

maya (support): I can reproduce a similar export locally by running the scheduled export job for an org set to Asia/Tokyo. Looks like the export pipeline truncates timestamps to UTC midnight instead of using the org's timezone setting for the daily bucket. Tagging @jon (platform) to inspect the export job code path for legacy vs new exports.

jon (platform): digging in the export service logs — exporting job id `export-789` has this transform: `DATE_TRUNC('day', timestamp)` with no timezone applied, which defaults to UTC. There's a guard in the new export endpoint to pass `org_tz` into the SQL but scheduled exports still hit the legacy path. Repro steps I used:

```
# mimic scheduled export call
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/usage/export?org_id=acme-inc&range=2024-03-01_2024-03-12" -o export.csv
# then inspect first few rows
head -n 10 export.csv
```

jon (platform): Quick workaround: hit the export API with `tz=Asia/Tokyo` to force the timezone-aware bucketing (new endpoint supports this), e.g. `?tz=Asia/Tokyo`. I'll open ENG-1234 for the scheduled/legacy export path so we can get parity.

kevin (billing): Important: our invoicing pipeline currently picks daily buckets from the exported CSV for some back-office reconciliations. If the CSV is UTC-bucketed but customers expect their org timezone, that could create apparent day-of-use mismatches. We should pause scheduled exports for affected orgs until we have a fix or re-run corrected exports for the past 30 days.

maya (support): Sara — can you confirm affected date range so we can scope a re-run and potential credits? Also: did you notice this only for scheduled exports or when you press "Download" manually too?

sara-acme: Affected window is 2024-03-01 -> 2024-03-12. It happened for both scheduled and manual downloads when we used the Console download button earlier today.

jon (platform): Ok creating ENG-1234: "scheduled exports use UTC day truncation instead of org timezone". Priority P2. I pushed a small fix in staging that threads `org_tz` through the legacy job. We'll validate with the sample org.

incident-bot: [automated] Ticket ENG-1234 created by jon (platform). Priority: P2.

maya (support): Interim mitigation options for customers:
1) We can stop scheduled exports for the org (prevent further bad CSVs).
2) Re-run exports for the affected date range with `tz=Asia/Tokyo` to produce corrected CSVs and compare diffs.
3) If billing reconciliation already ran against the bad CSVs, billing can re-calc credits after we provide corrected files (tagging @kevin).

maya (support): Sample re-run command for support to run on behalf of the customer:
```
# run corrected export with timezone override
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/usage/export?org_id=acme-inc&range=2024-03-01_2024-03-12&tz=Asia/Tokyo" \
  -o acme-corrected-2024-03-01_0312.csv
```

maya (support): Sara — we'll pause your scheduled exports now and kick off a corrected re-run. Expect CSV within ~30 mins. We'll follow up with a stitched diff and a proposed credit if billing was affected.

sara-acme: Thanks — please pause and re-run. We'll hold off opening a billing dispute until we see the corrected files. Really appreciate the quick response :pray:

jon (platform): Patch merged to staging. I'll run the integration job against `acme-inc` in staging and send you a preview. Plan to deploy to prod during the next maintenance window (2024-03-15 03:00 UTC) unless we see regressions.

kevin (billing): I'll prepare a reconciliation run for Mar 1-12 once we have corrected CSVs. If there are differences that affect billed usage, we'll apply credits and follow up with the customer.

maya (support): Follow-up ticket created in Support: SUP-5621 to track customer comms + delivery of corrected exports.

sara-acme: Sounds good, thanks everyone. Please DM me when the corrected CSV is available so I can confirm before billing changes.

maya (support): Will do — I'll post here when the re-run completes and attach the corrected CSV for you to validate.
